newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - June 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Agriculture Minister Hassan Abou Ayoub forecasts wheat harvest down by two-thirds to 3.3 million tonnes and expects to import up to 2.5 tonnes of soft wheat for the 1997-98 season.

- Banks attribute investors' wait-and-see attitude to a bad agricultural performance and say they will not be able to assess impact of interest rate cuts before one or two years. According to the banks, obstacles to growth are linked to the global economic environment affecting companies.
- General Confederation of Moroccan Businesses voices concern about delay in customs reform during meeting with Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj.

- New York bank Laidlaw and Co says in report on emerging markets that economic reforms have triggered stock exchange bullish trend for the first quarter of 1997. It expects the market to slow down which it says is a sign of maturity.
- Subscriptions for 20 percent of Imiter silver mine will be on sale from June 9-13.
- The United Nations Development Programme backs environment protection projects in Morocco.
